Good quality machine. Makes ice in like 5 minutes! - This makes the cutest little ice cubs, I think they're perfect if you are someone who eats ice. For an ice chest you'll probably be working at it for a while as this thing makes a handful of cubes every few minutes. The thing I love about this ice maker is it has a smaller profile than many of them I've seen. Many are much larger and bulkier. This one's not too bad at all. After using this thing a few times I can say that we love it! Seems to be well made and works perfectly.

The small ice and large ice are the exact same size, the large ice just stays on the metal rods longer so they become thicker. Both of them come out thin enough I can put them in my hand and just crush them completely. I honestly love this ice and am very happy with this!

To make Ice you just fill the bottom reservoir with water up to it's "Max" fill line which is marked "Max" and then it sucks water from that up to the top reservoir where the metal rods are cooled to the point that ice starts forming on them. Once the ice is ready it will drop the ice and the little motorized scoop will scoop it down into the little ice tray. Very easy to use and fun to watch!

This is an issue because of the flawed design of the bottom rack in the Whirlpool/Maytag/etc. dishwasher where the rollers press down on the splash shields when the rack is rolled in and out to load/unload. This pressure seems to be why these splash shields fail so often. Since these don't flex as well as the originals, they are prone to be dislodged when the rack rolls over them. This can cause leakage. It can also cause the shields to fail even sooner since they don't flex as well. As a matter of interest, I recently checked the current models of the Whirlpool, etc. dishwashers and they don't use this splash shield at all but have redesigned the door and the door seal. I guess the engineers realized this was a constantly failing part.
